title: sre-weekly-update-2026-08-08
content:
SRE Weekly Update — Week of 2026-08-08

Owner: Aisha Patel (SRE Manager)
Contributors: Ethan Kim, Priya Shah, Marcus Green, Lena Volkova
Distribution: eng-sre, platform-engineering, site-reliability, product-hosted-api

Summary
- Quiet week for system-wide outages; one Sev2 degradation and multiple short-lived degradations on the inference gateway during traffic spikes.
- Error budgets: inference-api still within budget but routing-service has <10% remaining for the quarter — follow-up actions below.
- Runbook updates merged for cache warmup and model rollout pilot.
- On-call rotation: handoff completed on 2026-08-07 at 09:00 UTC. Primary for next week: Ethan Kim, Secondary: Priya Shah.

Incidents
1) Sev2: inference-gateway increased 5xx rate during model rollout window (2026-07-31 03:20 - 2026-07-31 04:05 UTC)
   - Incident ID: PDIJ-2026-07-31 (PagerDuty) / JIRA-SRE-4523
   - Impact: ~8% of requests in us-west-2 returned 5xx (model shard cold-start + a buggy autoscaler config that allowed a surge of unhealthy pods). Upstream retries caused queuing and elevated latencies for ~45 minutes.
   - Mitigation: Reverted rollout (model-v2 -> model-v1), temporarily increased replica limits to absorb traffic, patched autoscaler config to add a health-probe backoff.
   - Post-incident actions: postmortem started; root cause narrowed to missed health probe behavior in the autoscaler when new containers hit heavy disk I/O during model warmup. Action items: adjust probe timing (PR: infra#1284), add canary testing for cold-start heavy models, add metrics for model warmup time to Prometheus.

2) Short degradations: KV-cache eviction storms during heavy prefix caching (2026-08-04 14:10 - 14:25 UTC)
   - Impact: small percentage of requests experienced cache misses -> increased token cost and latency for a subset of reserved traffic.
   - Mitigation: Manual cache size bump and temporary pinning of high-QPS keys.
   - Follow-up: tune eviction policy and implement gradual cache warmup for traffic spikes. Runbook note appended (Confluence Runbook Index).

SLOs & Metrics
- inference-api availability (p99 success): 99.992% this week (target 99.95%) — good
- routing-service error budget remaining for quarter: ~9% — risk threshold exceeded for proactive remediation
- request latency (p50/p90/p99) stable for most services; tail latency spikes correlated with garbage collection pauses on a small fleet of model-serving hosts. Action: SRE + infra to investigate GC tuning and upgrade Java runtime on those hosts.

On-call handoffs
- Handoff completed 2026-08-07 09:00 UTC (Aisha -> Ethan)
- Notes for on-call:
   - Watch for increased errors during any model rollouts; prefer gradual ramp and enable canary traffic only after warmup completes.
   - If routing-service error budget falls <5%, throttle non-critical background jobs and contact product-hosted-api to pause non-urgent experiments.
   - Reminder: run the health-probe validation script before any autoscaler change (scripts/health_probe_check).

Runbook & Ops changes
- Merged: cache-warmup-runbook (Confluence) — includes step-by-step for manual warmup and a script to pre-populate top prefixes.
- Merged: autoscaler-health-probe-fix PR (infra#1284) — adjust backoff and add prestart health delay for heavy-model containers.
- Added metric: model_warmup_seconds (Prometheus) — alerts at 2x expected warmup for model families.

Action Items (owners and ETA)
- infra: deploy autoscaler health-probe fix to prod by 2026-08-10 (owner: Marcus Green)
- eng-serving-runtime: instrument model_warmup_seconds and publish dashboard by 2026-08-12 (owner: Priya Shah)
- SRE: create canary checklist for model rollouts and integrate into rollout pipeline by 2026-08-15 (owner: Ethan Kim)
- SRE+Platform: GC tuning experiment on problem hosts; experiment summary by 2026-08-14 (owner: Lena Volkova)

Follow-ups / Postmortems
- PDIJ-2026-07-31 -> JIRA-SRE-4523: postmortem draft in progress, expected review 2026-08-09. Main follow-ups: autoscaler probe timing, canary policy for heavy models, and cache eviction tuning.
- JIRA-SRE-4530: ticket opened to throttle background experiments when routing error budget below threshold.

Risks & Blockers
- Routing-service error budget trending low: if not addressed, may force rollback of non-critical features and restrict capacity for Dedicated customers during next month.
- Dependence on infra team for autoscaler fix (PR merged but needs deployment window coordinated with platform team).

Planned Work Next Week
- Deploy autoscaler patch during low-traffic window (coord with platform ops).
- Finish model_warmup metrics and dashboard; start 1-week warmup data collection.
- Run GC tuning experiments and evaluate impact on tail latency.
- Review canary checklist and run a simulated canary with staging traffic.

Notes & Loose Items
- Reminder: update on-call runbook with PagerDuty escalation steps for model-related incidents (owner: Aisha).
- We observed increased noisy neighbor incidents in us-east-1 during HPC burst tests; will coordinate with partners to propose relocation policy for heavy jobs.

Attachments / Links
- Runbook index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+Index
- Incident: PagerDuty PDIJ-2026-07-31 (link above)
- Postmortem draft: JIRA-SRE-4523
- Autoscaler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284

Questions for Owners
- Marcus: can we get a firm deploy window for the autoscaler change this week?
- Priya/Ethan: do we have any additional warmup telemetry from staging that indicates similar cold-start behavior?

Sign-off
- Aisha Patel (SRE Manager)
